about: THE HELD-OUT SET. Do not tune against it.
The other question set was written by the same person who then changed the ranking
rules to score better on it. That is marking your own homework, and the number it
produces cannot answer the only question that matters: does this work on a codebase
and a phrasing nobody had in mind while writing the code?
These forty were written on 2026-09-07 by four separate agents, one per codebase,
each with a clean context and each forbidden from looking at graph-paat at all --
not its source, not its existing questions, not its output. They worked only from
the library's own source, and every answer was verified to exist as a node.
The rule that keeps this honest: score it, write the number down, and do not change
a ranking rule because of what it says. If a change is made for the other set, this
one is re-scored afterwards to see whether the gain was real or was overfitting.

transformers.q: how does a tokenizer turn a list of chat messages into the prompt string
transformers.why: tokenization_utils_base.py:L2914 - read the body: it takes a conversation of role/content dicts, reads the tokenizer's chat_template attribute and renders it, optionally tokenizing the result

transformers.q: how does a slow tokenizer find user added special strings inside raw text before splitting words
transformers.why: tokenization_python.py:L45 - the class docstring says it is built out of the added tokens and used to split on them in one pass; confirmed the tokenizer calls self.tokens_trie.split(text) at tokenization_python.py:L644

transformers.q: how are the least likely words discarded so the remaining ones add up to a set probability
transformers.why: generation/logits_process.py:L468 - its __call__ sorts the logits, takes a cumulative softmax and masks out everything below the 1 - top_p cut-off, which is exactly nucleus filtering

transformers.q: where are the keys and values from earlier tokens kept so they are not recomputed at every step
transformers.why: cache_utils.py:L906 - docstring: a cache that grows as more tokens are generated and is the default for generative models; it holds one key/value layer per decoder layer and is the object passed as past_key_values

transformers.q: how is the mask that hides future positions built for a decoder
transformers.why: masking_utils.py:L831 - builds the causal mask for the configured attention implementation from the attention mask, cache position and cache; grep shows 133 modeling_*.py files call it

transformers.q: how do a model's dense layers get swapped for low bit versions when loading a quantized checkpoint
transformers.why: integrations/bitsandbytes.py:L157 - walks named_modules and substitutes each nn.Linear/Conv1D with bnb.nn.Linear8bitLt or bnb.nn.Linear4bit according to the quantization config

transformers.q: where is the loop over epochs and batches that fine tuning actually runs
transformers.why: trainer.py:L2225 - builds the train dataloader, handles resume state, then runs `for epoch in range(epochs_trained, num_train_epochs)` with the gradient accumulation chunking inside; Trainer.train only sets up and delegates here

transformers.q: how are training batches prepared for masked language model pretraining
transformers.why: data/data_collator.py:L619 - pads a batch dynamically and, via its torch_mask_tokens at L796, selects tokens with mlm_probability then applies the 80/10/10 mask, random, keep split and sets non selected labels to -100

transformers.q: which model gets used when someone asks for a task without naming a checkpoint
transformers.why: pipelines/base.py:L275 - reads targeted_task['default'] and returns the default model plus revision; called from pipelines/__init__.py:L783 in the branch where no model was supplied

transformers.q: how do weights from a downloaded checkpoint end up in the right places inside the model
transformers.why: core_model_loading.py:L972 - renames each checkpoint key by the weight mapping rules, applies conversion ops (chunk, concatenate, merge experts, transpose, rope permute) and sets the resulting tensors on the modules; modeling_utils.py:L4182 in _load_pretrained_model is its only caller

sympy.q: what combines like terms when a sum is built
sympy.why: core/add.py:L198 is Add.flatten (class Add starts at L93); its body keeps a term->coeff dict and does terms[s] += c at L321, which is where two equal terms in a sum get merged into one coefficient

sympy.q: how are repeated pieces of a large expression pulled out and named once
sympy.why: simplify/cse_main.py:L728 defines cse, documented as performing common subexpression elimination and returning (Symbol, expression) replacement pairs plus the reduced expressions; codegen/ast.py:L746 only wraps it for a code block

sympy.q: how does the library work out which method fits a differential equation
sympy.why: solvers/ode/ode.py:L819, whose docstring says it returns the tuple of possible classifications ordered so the first is the one dsolve uses by default

sympy.q: which routine finds an antiderivative the way a student would on paper
sympy.why: integrals/manualintegrate.py:L2115, docstring: computes an indefinite integral 'using an algorithm that resembles what a student would do by hand'; Integral._eval_integral calls it as the manual method

sympy.q: how are the eigenvalues of a matrix computed
sympy.why: matrices/eigen.py:L80 holds the actual computation (roots of the characteristic polynomial, error_when_incomplete/rational/multiple handling); MatrixBase.eigenvals at matrices/matrixbase.py:L3330 is a one-line delegation to it

sympy.q: how is a ratio of polynomials split into a sum of simpler fractions
sympy.why: polys/partfrac.py:L15, docstring: 'Compute partial fraction decomposition of a rational function', offering the undetermined coefficients method and Bronstein's full algorithm

sympy.q: how do I render an expression as latex markup
sympy.why: printing/latex.py:L2968, the public function documented as converting the given expression to a LaTeX string, with all the printer settings as keywords

sympy.q: how is an expression rewritten using facts already known about its symbols
sympy.why: assumptions/refine.py:L11; it recurses over args and dispatches to _eval_refine / handlers_dict, and its docstring contrasts it with simplify as the one that uses assumptions (Basic.refine at core/basic.py:L1958 just calls it)

sympy.q: how do you change a quantity into different units
sympy.why: physics/units/util.py:L52, documented as converting an expression so its units are expressed as factors of the target units, e.g. convert_to(mile, kilometer); Quantity.convert_to at physics/units/quantities.py:L119 delegates here

sympy.q: how do I turn a formula into a fast numeric python callable
sympy.why: utilities/lambdify.py:L198, docstring: 'Convert a SymPy expression into a function that allows for fast numeric evaluation', generating and exec-ing the function source

pandas.q: what turns a path or url into an open stream and deals with compression on the way
pandas.why: io/common.py:L665 is the real body under three typing overloads; it calls _get_filepath_or_buffer for local/remote paths and then wraps the result in gzip/bz2/zip/zstd according to the compression argument, and every reader and writer opens its target through it

pandas.q: where does assigning a value into a selected part of a frame actually take effect
pandas.why: core/indexing.py:L1786; the shared __setitem__ at core/indexing.py:L884 ends with iloc._setitem_with_indexer(indexer, value, self.name), so both label and positional assignment funnel into this one method, which then splits the write across blocks

pandas.q: how does pandas work out which rows belong to which group
pandas.why: core/groupby/grouper.py:L846; its docstring says it creates the BaseGrouper that is the internal mapping of how to build the group indexers, and GroupBy.__init__ calls it at core/groupby/groupby.py:L1331 to interpret keys, levels, functions or Grouper objects

pandas.q: when two tables are merged on a key, what figures out which rows on each side line up
pandas.why: core/reshape/merge.py:L1693 factorizes the left and right key arrays and returns the pair of positional indexers into each side; _MergeOperation._get_join_indexers at core/reshape/merge.py:L1120 is a one-line delegation to it

pandas.q: how is a frequency table of two columns computed
pandas.why: core/reshape/pivot.py:L578, docstring 'Compute a simple cross tabulation of two (or more) factors... computes a frequency table of the factors'; it is the only implementation and has no DataFrame method delegating to it

pandas.q: what enforces the cap on how many values in a row may be filled
pandas.why: core/missing.py:L1079, docstring 'Get indexers of values that won't be filled because they exceed the limits'; _interpolate_1d calls it at core/missing.py:L495-L500 to build the set of gaps left untouched for forward, backward and both directions

pandas.q: how are strings converted into real timestamps
pandas.why: core/tools/datetimes.py:L678 is the implementation under three overload stubs; the body dispatches scalars, Series, DataFrames and list-likes through convert_listlike and _assemble_from_unit_mappings (core/tools/datetimes.py:L1050 onward)

pandas.q: given several different column types, what works out the single type they can all become
pandas.why: core/dtypes/cast.py:L1444 is the implementation under three overloads; docstring 'Find a common data type among the given dtypes', handling both numpy dtypes and extension dtypes

pandas.q: what merges the separate chunks holding columns of the same type into one
pandas.why: core/internals/managers.py:L2278, docstring 'Merge blocks having same dtype, exclude non-consolidating blocks'; it groups blocks by their consolidate key and is what _consolidate_inplace (core/internals/managers.py:L1801) calls, with _merge_blocks as its per-group helper

pandas.q: how does pandas decide which library actually draws a chart
pandas.why: plotting/_core.py:L1920; it reads the backend argument or the plotting.backend option, lazily imports and caches that module, and its docstring says the returned module provides the top-level plot method that does the drawing

scipy.q: how do I fit a function with unknown parameters to measured data points
scipy.why: optimize/_minpack_py.py:L590, docstring reads 'Use non-linear least squares to fit a function, f, to data' and the body builds p0/sigma and drives leastsq or least_squares, returning popt and the covariance.

scipy.q: how is a system of ordinary differential equations advanced through time from a starting state
scipy.why: integrate/_ivp/ivp.py:L159, 'Solve an initial value problem for a system of ODEs'; the body runs the while loop calling solver.step() until t_span is covered, so it is the driver, not a helper.

scipy.q: how do I interpolate scattered data in several dimensions
scipy.why: interpolate/_ndgriddata.py:L170, docstring 'Convenience function for interpolating unstructured data in multiple dimensions'; it dispatches to the Nearest/Linear/CloughTocher ND interpolators and is the documented entry point.

scipy.q: how do I subtract a slow drift from a recorded signal
scipy.why: signal/_signaltools.py:L4120, 'Remove linear or constant trend along axis from data' — the body subtracts a least-squares linear (or mean) fit, optionally per break-point segment.

scipy.q: how do I solve a linear system whose matrix is sparse
scipy.why: sparse/linalg/_dsolve/linsolve.py:L134, 'Solve the sparse linear system Ax=b'; it converts A to CSC/CSR and calls SuperLU or UMFPACK, so it is the sparse direct solver entry point.

scipy.q: how do I get the distance between every pair of points from two separate sets
scipy.why: spatial/distance.py:L2793, 'Compute distance between each pair of the two collections of inputs' — takes XA and XB, unlike pdist which works within one set.

scipy.q: how is a confidence interval built by resampling the observed data with replacement
scipy.why: stats/_resampling.py:L281, 'Compute a two-sided bootstrap confidence interval of a statistic'; the body loops over batches calling _bootstrap_resample, then forms the percentile/basic/BCa interval and returns BootstrapResult.

scipy.q: how is a matrix factored into an orthogonal part and an upper triangular part
scipy.why: linalg/_decomp_qr.py:L28, 'Calculate the decomposition A = Q R where Q is unitary/orthogonal and R upper triangular'; the body calls the LAPACK geqrf/geqp3 and orgqr routines and assembles Q and R per mode.

scipy.q: how are observations merged step by step into a nested hierarchy of groups
scipy.why: cluster/hierarchy.py:L814, 'Perform hierarchical/agglomerative clustering'; the body picks and calls _hierarchy.mst_single_linkage / nn_chain / fast_linkage and returns the (n-1)x4 merge matrix Z.

scipy.q: how do I read a MATLAB data file
scipy.why: io/matlab/_mio.py:L87, 'Load MATLAB file' — opens the .mat file, builds the version-appropriate MatFile reader and returns the variables dict.
